questions.stem: R = {1, 2, 3} and S = {2, 3, 4}. What is R − S?
questions.explain: R − S keeps the members of R that are not in S. Only 1 qualifies.

questions.stem: The rows (age, dept) are (22, CS), (19, CS), (25, EE) and (30, CS). How many rows satisfy age > 20 AND dept = CS?
questions.explain: A row needs both conditions. (22, CS) and (30, CS) pass. (19, CS) fails the age test and (25, EE) fails the dept test.

questions.stem: R = {1, 2, 3} and S = {2, 3, 4}. How many pairs (r, s) with r in R and s in S are there?
questions.explain: Every element of R pairs with every element of S: 3 × 3 = 9.

questions.stem: Many employees work in one department. Where does the foreign key dept_id go?
questions.explain: The foreign key goes on the "many" side. Each employee row stores the id of its one department.

questions.stem: roll_no is the primary key of a table. At most how many rows can have roll_no = 5?
questions.explain: A primary key value identifies a single row, so it cannot repeat.
